source.title: Gradient Flossing: Improving Gradient Descent through Dynamic Control of Jacobians

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents reading.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports experiments on recurrent networks and synthetic long-horizon tasks, testing gradient trainability with a new Jacobian-regularization method. This is a new setting relative to the listed claim versions, which focus mainly on feedforward networks and benchmark classification.
record.gate_note: The paper's results concern recurrent networks, Lyapunov exponents, gradient propagation and synthetic temporal tasks. They do not test the listed CIFAR classification claims, teacher-student local minima, feedforward depth, initialization comparisons as named in V4, learning-rate stability, or batch normalization. Rows capture gradient-flossing effects on the directly measured gradient and trainability outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study uses critical and orthogonal initialization as starting recipes and evaluates its own Lyapunov-exponent regularization method in RNNs. Its results concern temporal credit assignment, not the feedforward initialization, depth, classification, local-minimum, learning-rate or normalization comparisons specified in V1–V6. Orthogonal initialization is a control condition, not a test of V4's stated comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that regularizing Lyapunov exponents improves gradient propagation, convergence speed and accuracy on synthetic long-horizon RNN tasks. Early episodes during task training can extend the learnable horizon beyond preflossing alone, while continued flossing can harm accuracy. These conclusions do not establish V1–V6.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces gradient flossing, an added Lyapunov-exponent regularization procedure for recurrent networks, and evaluates synthetic sequence tasks rather than the listed classification or feedforward-network recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies with task delay and number of Lyapunov exponents flossed; preflossing versus flossing during training changes outcomes; continued flossing throughout all training can be detrimental; results also include orthogonal initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Preflossing extends the delays that vanilla RNNs can learn; additional flossing during early task training improves performance on harder temporal and spatial XOR tasks, including with orthogonal initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lyapunov-exponent regularization can improve convergence and long-horizon task performance in the tested RNNs.

fits_no_version.finding: Harder streaming tasks require more flossed exponents; preflossing all exponents still fails on the hardest tasks, and continued flossing can repeatedly disrupt learned accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefits of gradient flossing depend on the number of regularized directions and the intervention schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Flossing increases long-horizon gradient norms, and gradient growth precedes above-chance accuracy across network realizations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient flossing improves long-horizon error propagation in the tested recurrent networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Flossing controls selected Lyapunov exponents and reduces long-term Jacobian conditioning problems in recurrent networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selected recurrent-network Lyapunov exponents can be regularized to improve long-term Jacobian conditioning.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix G reports that orthogonally initialized spatial-XOR networks with either flossing schedule bridge d = 70 after 10000 epochs, motivating the shorter 5000-epoch comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Orthogonal initialization may complement gradient flossing on long-horizon recurrent tasks; this does not establish the stated feedforward initialization claim.

record.code_released: URL not reproduced in supplied text; example implementation said to be available via a link.
record.problems: The experiments use synthetic recurrent-network tasks rather than CIFAR classification benchmarks. The task stream couples delay with the number of values that must be remembered, as the authors note. Several reported accuracy patterns are described through figures without exact values in the text; some passages do not state run counts.
record.rows_left_out: Lyapunov-exponent control experiments and condition-number measurements are described in the paper, but do not directly test any listed version. Additional repeated realizations and plotted accuracy curves are not separately extracted where no exact text result is stated; see Figures 1-5, 8-14 and appendices.

untested.parts: All parts: training classification error in sufficiently large CNNs on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and model-size or training-recipe qualifications.
All parts: spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and the effect of extra student neurons.
All parts: depth degradation in plain CNNs, identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization and normalization-free residual exceptions.

All parts of the stated feedforward claim: activation-matched initialization, trainable depth, orthogonal versus equal-variance Gaussian initialization in deep tanh networks, and 10000-layer plain CNNs.
All parts: learning rates relative to the initial stability threshold, loss-curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability behavior and divergence.
All parts: batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6 because their measures fit no listed version; this does not dispute the reported flossing effects. The rows describe the study's own method performance and should not be counted as evidence for these versions. No additional result requiring a version-linked missing entry was identified.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification, random or corrupted labels, model size, early stopping and regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual feedforward CNN depth comparisons, shortcut effects, and the cited special initialization or normalization-free residual recipes.
The listed feedforward initialization comparisons, activation-matched initializations, deep tanh networks and 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks.
Squared-loss learning-rate sweeps above the stability limit, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence conditions.
Batch-normalization comparisons on MNIST, CIFAR-10 or ImageNet, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup residual networks.

rows.subject: Vanilla RNN
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flossing before task training on the delayed copy task
rows.measure: Test loss during training and mean final test loss across delay difficulty
rows.value: Gradient flossing substantially improves performance; reliably trained for d = 40, while without flossing networks fail to train reliably beyond d = 20
rows.uncertainty: Median across 5 network realizations in the time-course; 20% and 80% percentiles for difficulty sweep
rows.note: Synthetic delayed-copy regression task, not classification benchmarks.
rows.check: The flossing performance comparison does not measure any listed version. Section 6 states k = 40 for the copy task, but Figure 3's caption states k = 75; preserve this source inconsistency.

rows.subject: Vanilla RNN
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flossing before task training on delayed temporal XOR
rows.measure: Test accuracy as a function of delay
rows.value: Preflossing improves trainability, but accuracy still goes to chance level for d = 70; baseline falls to chance level for d ≥ 40
rows.uncertainty: Mean across 20 network realizations; individual realizations shown
rows.note: Binary XOR task. The text explicitly identifies chance-level accuracy for the stated delays.
rows.check: The reported improvement and remaining chance-level performance concern preflossing on an RNN task, not any listed version.

rows.subject: Vanilla RNN
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flossing before and during task training on delayed temporal XOR

conditions.value: 500 epochs before training and again after 500 task-training epochs

rows.value: > 80% at d = 70 with flossing during training
rows.uncertainty: Mean across 20 network realizations; individual realizations shown
rows.note: Outcome is test accuracy on a synthetic temporal task.
rows.check: The greater-than-80% accuracy is supported by Section 7, but measures the study's flossing intervention rather than a listed version.

rows.subject: Vanilla RNN
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flossing before and during task training on delayed spatial XOR

conditions.value: 500 epochs before training and during training

rows.measure: Test accuracy as a function of delay
rows.value: Preflossing improves performance but starts failing for d > 60; networks also flossed during training solve more difficult tasks
rows.uncertainty: Mean across realizations; 20% and 80% percentiles in Figure 4D
rows.note: The text describes direction and difficulty boundary but does not state the exact accuracy for each delay.
rows.check: This combines preflossing limitations with improvement from flossing during training; it cannot receive a single partial state against a listed version. Figure 4B inherits 20 realizations from panel A, so the run count is available for that time course.

rows.subject: Vanilla RNN
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flossing during training while varying the number of flossed Lyapunov exponents

conditions.value: larger delay d requires more Lyapunov exponents flossed

rows.measure: Test accuracy by number of flossed Lyapunov exponents and delay
rows.baseline: Fewer flossed Lyapunov exponents under the same task and delay
rows.value: More Lyapunov exponents have to be flossed to achieve 100% accuracy as tasks become more difficult
rows.uncertainty: 25% and 75% percentiles shown; means and individual simulations shown
rows.note: The authors qualify that the streaming task also requires remembering more values at longer delays.
rows.check: The number of regularized Lyapunov exponents is an intervention parameter, not network width or another quantity specified by V1–V6.

rows.subject: Vanilla RNN
rows.operation_detail: Preflossing only while varying the number of flossed Lyapunov exponents

conditions.value: most difficult delayed temporal XOR tasks

rows.measure: Ability to solve the most difficult tasks, reported through test accuracy
rows.value: Even if all N Lyapunov exponents were flossed, they were not able to solve the most difficult tasks
rows.note: The paper says preflossing cannot replace gradient flossing during training.
rows.check: Failure to solve the hardest tasks does not establish absence of improvement over baseline. The text establishes that preflossing alone is insufficient, not that a listed version's effect is absent.

rows.subject: Vanilla RNN
rows.operation_detail: Repeated gradient-flossing episodes throughout all training epochs on delayed temporal XOR

conditions.value: floss throughout training every 100 training epochs for 500 flossing epochs

rows.baseline: Early training flossing at epochs e ∈ {0, 100, 200, 300, 400}; no flossing
rows.value: Accuracy drops close to chance level after each flossing episode, recovers quickly between episodes, and never reaches 100%
rows.note: The authors state continued flossing can be detrimental to task accuracy.
rows.check: Continued flossing harms accuracy relative to early-only flossing. This is not a reversal of any listed version, and the detrimental comparison should not be generalized to the no-flossing baseline.

rows.subject: Vanilla RNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured gradient norm with respect to initial conditions during delayed temporal XOR training
rows.value: Each flossing episode causes the norm to spike, surpassing values larger than 10^-2
rows.uncertainty: One out of ten network realizations shown with solid line; other nine transparent
rows.note: The paper describes this gradient measurement as evidence that flossing boosts long-horizon gradient norm.
rows.check: The gradient-norm increase measures the flossing intervention, not an initialization comparison. The schedule includes epoch 500 in Figure 8's caption but ends at 400 in the surrounding prose; flag the inconsistency.

rows.subject: Vanilla RNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured test accuracy alongside gradient norm during delayed temporal XOR training
rows.measure: Test accuracy relative to chance level
rows.value: Test accuracy surpasses chance level after gradient norm grows macroscopically; reported consistently across numerous network realizations
rows.locator: Appendix D, Figure 8B-D and surrounding text
rows.note: Test accuracy is reported as a result associated with the intervention, but no exact final percentage is stated in this passage.
rows.check: The association between gradient growth and subsequent test accuracy does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: Vanilla RNN
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flossing during training with orthogonal weight initialization on delayed temporal XOR

conditions.value: 500 epochs before task training and again after 500 task-training epochs

rows.value: > 80% at d = 70 with gradient flossing during training; baseline falls to chance for d ≥ 40 and preflossing remains close to chance at d = 70
rows.uncertainty: Mean across network realizations; individual realizations shown
rows.note: Orthogonal initialization is stated as the condition; run count is not stated.
rows.check: Orthogonal initialization is held fixed while flossing varies. This does not compare orthogonal and Gaussian initialization as required by V4.

rows.subject: Vanilla RNN
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flossing before and during task training with orthogonal initialization on delayed spatial XOR
rows.measure: Test accuracy as a function of delay
rows.value: Preflossing improves performance but starts failing for long delays d > 60; networks also flossed during training solve more difficult tasks
rows.uncertainty: Mean across realizations; 25% and 75% percentiles shown
rows.note: Authors note they used 5000 epochs here, compared with 10000 epochs for Gaussian initialization.
rows.check: This measures flossing under orthogonal initialization rather than V4's initialization comparison. Appendix G also reports that at 10000 epochs both preflossing and before-and-during flossing bridge d = 70; the stated limitation applies to the 5000-epoch evaluation.
